market_view: South African shares had a weak week, with the JSE All Share down 2.6% and the Top 40 down 3.1% as gold and platinum fell about 4%, although the rand held firm at R16.48/$ and the SA 10-year eased to about 8.8% even as September CPI ticked up to 4.5%, above the 3% target, ahead of the 19 Nov MPC. In New York the S&P 500 slipped 0.5% and the Nasdaq 0.7% while September US CPI rose to 3.7%, keeping the 10-year Treasury near 5% and the focus on the Fed's 28 Oct decision and a heavy week of big-tech results. Brent above $110 a barrel keeps inflation risks alive while softer precious metals and flat iron ore weigh on SA miners, so investors should expect continued volatility and favour balance-sheet strength over stretched valuations.
